description: The window showing a CONTROL PLANE's own page. A plane can live on any host, so unlike apps/server/desktop's loopback window this one's origin cannot be enumerated here, which is why the scope is a wildcard and why the narrowness has to live in the COMMAND instead. It gets exactly one: desktop_open_in_browser, which takes a PATH (no scheme, no protocol-relative '//host', no backslash, no whitespace or control characters) and joins it onto the origin windows.rs's PlanePin already holds, the same value that window's navigation guard enforces. So a compromised plane page can open a page of ITSELF in the person's browser, which they could do by typing the address. No node_* verb, no plugin permission, and no core:default: everything that drives the subshell CLI is granted to the bundled `node` window and to nothing else. The wildcard scope is deliberate and is NOT a widening of who may invoke: any page loaded in this window is the plane the person chose, because on_navigation pins the window to that origin. Adding a second permission here is a change to the trust model; see docs/security.md, and the pin in ui/src/__tests__/ipc-acl.test.ts.
